chunks: Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Hisham, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

The end of an orphan’s state of orphanhood is puberty, and that is his full strength. But if he reaches puberty and no sound maturity is perceived in him, and he is foolish or weak, then his guardian should withhold his wealth from him.

key_terms.رُشْدُهُ: sound judgment and right maturity in managing affairs
key_terms.يُتْمِ: the state of being an orphan

ai.seo_question: When does an orphan cease to be legally considered an orphan, and when may their wealth still be withheld?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that orphanhood, in legal terms, ends with puberty. However, the transfer of wealth is not based on puberty alone; if sound judgment is not evident and the person is foolish or weak-minded, the guardian is to continue withholding the property.
